title: Linkability of sensor data
description: Wearable device links multiple telemetry data points (heart rate, GPS, timestamps) to uniquely identify the user across contexts.
assumptions: Device processes and correlates data streams without user consent for linkage.

title: Inference of sensitive health information
description: Device infers sensitive health conditions (e.g., stress, illness) from continuous heart rate and activity patterns.
assumptions: Telemetry data contains patterns correlatable to health states.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure
description: Sensor data stored on wearable device may be accessed by unauthorized parties due to weak security controls.
assumptions: Device lacks encryption or access controls for stored telemetry.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Sensor telemetry could be altered or corrupted during transmission from user to device.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks integrity verification mechanisms.

title: User unaware of data collection scope
description: User may not fully understand the extent of continuous monitoring (e.g., GPS tracking, health metrics) when wearing the device.
assumptions: Privacy notices are unclear or not prominently displayed.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Companion app may share synced sensor data (GPS traces, device ID) with third parties without user consent, violating data minimality principles.
assumptions: App has undisclosed third-party integrations or data-sharing agreements.

title: Identifiability via Metadata in Transit
description: Device ID and timestamps in the data flow can be used to identify the user if intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Data flow lacks encryption or obfuscation of identifying metadata.

title: Linkability of Sensor Data with User Profiles
description: App combines wearable sensor data with other user data (e.g., account info) to create detailed behavioral profiles, increasing re-identification risk.
assumptions: App stores and processes additional user data beyond the synced sensor batches.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Wearable device transmits data without clear user notification about what data is shared, with whom, or for what purpose.
assumptions: Device lacks transparent data-sharing indicators or consent mechanisms.

title: Unauthorized Access to Data in Transit
description: Sensor data (GPS traces, exercise sessions) could be intercepted during transmission if communication channels are not encrypted.
assumptions: Data flow uses unencrypted or weakly secured communication protocols.

title: Health data aggregation reveals sensitive patterns
description: The companion app aggregates calorie intake, meal, and weight entries over time, potentially revealing sensitive health patterns, lifestyle information, or medical conditions beyond what the user intended to share.
assumptions: App stores and processes multiple entries over time

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: Personal health data (calories, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate security controls at the app, data breaches, or improper sharing with third parties.
assumptions: App may have security vulnerabilities or share data with third parties

title: User unaware of data usage beyond app functionality
description: The user may not be fully aware of how their health data is being used, stored, or shared beyond the immediate app functionality, including potential secondary uses or data sharing with third parties.
assumptions: User may not read privacy policies or understand data processing implications

title: Health data enables user identification
description: The combination of weight, calorie intake, and meal patterns could potentially be used to identify or re-identify the user, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Health data patterns may be unique enough to identify individuals

title: User cannot control data processing after entry
description: Once health data is entered into the app, the user may have limited ability to control how it is processed, stored, or shared, including inability to delete or modify historical entries.
assumptions: App may not provide full data control mechanisms

title: Excessive Location Data Storage
description: The app stores continuous GPS traces with timestamps, potentially exceeding the data minimality principle by collecting more location data than necessary for its functionality.

title: Lack of User Awareness
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their precise location data is being continuously recorded and stored.

title: Identifiable Location Data
description: Stored GPS traces with timestamps can directly identify users without anonymization or pseudonymization.

title: Linkable Location Metadata
description: Transmission metadata (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers) could enable linking location data to user identity or other datasets.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Storage of sensitive location data may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) regarding purpose limitation and retention periods.

title: Health data linkability across sessions
description: The Health Analytics Service can link calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions to create comprehensive health profiles, potentially enabling identification of individuals through behavioral patterns even if individual records are anonymized.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to historical session data and can correlate patterns

title: Individual identification from health patterns
description: Health-condition analysis using calorie, weight, and exercise data could identify specific individuals through unique health patterns, especially when combined with other data sources or demographic information.
assumptions: Health patterns are sufficiently unique to enable identification

title: Implicit data disclosure to third parties
description: The Health Analytics Service may share derived health insights or raw health data with third parties (e.g., insurance companies, researchers, advertisers) without explicit user consent, constituting implicit data disclosure beyond the original collection purpose.
assumptions: Analytics service has partnerships or data-sharing agreements with external entities

title: User unawareness of cross-session health analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being analyzed across multiple sessions for health-condition analysis, violating the principle of informed consent and transparency.
assumptions: Privacy policy does not clearly disclose cross-session analytics

title: Non-compliance with health data regulations
description: Processing of health logs for analytics may not comply with applicable regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding sensitive health data, particularly if proper consent, purpose limitation, or data minimization principles are not followed.
assumptions: Analytics service operates in jurisdiction with health data protection laws

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Movement Patterns
description: Health Analytics Service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history, constituting explicit disclosure of personal data. This processing may violate the minimality principle if all derived patterns are not strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Analytics service processes location data to derive behavioral patterns as described in flow

title: Linkability Across Data Sources
description: Analytics service could link location history with other health data to create comprehensive user profiles, increasing linkability across different data sources and enabling more detailed user tracking.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to or can integrate with other health data sources

title: Unawareness of Pattern Derivation
description: Users may be unaware that their location history is being analyzed to derive movement patterns and daily routines, violating transparency and informed consent principles.
assumptions: Users were not explicitly informed about pattern derivation from location data

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Processing location history to derive behavioral patterns may not have proper legal basis or consent under GDPR or similar data protection regulations, especially if original consent was for different purposes.
assumptions: Processing may exceed original consent scope for location data collection

title: Identifiability Through Movement Patterns
description: Movement patterns derived from location history could identify individuals, especially when patterns are distinctive or combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to derive identifiable patterns

title: Data Disclosure from Storage to Analytics
description: Location History Store discloses personal location data to the analytics service, which may exceed the original purpose for which data was collected and stored.
assumptions: Data was originally collected for different purposes than analytics pattern derivation

title: Inferred health condition indicators reveal sensitive information
description: The app infers and displays eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals from user data. These inferred conditions may reveal sensitive health information the user did not explicitly provide or may not be aware is being deduced, potentially causing psychological harm or stigma.
assumptions: The inference algorithms are accurate enough to be meaningful; users may not understand how these indicators are derived

title: Sensitive health data visible to unauthorized observers
description: Health risk indicators displayed on the mobile app dashboard could be observed by others (shoulder surfing, screen sharing, device access), leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health information.
assumptions: User may use device in public or shared spaces; screen may not be adequately protected

title: User unaware of implications of displayed health indicators
description: Users may not fully understand what the risk indicators mean, how they were calculated, or the potential consequences of this information being visible or stored, leading to uninformed decisions about their health data.
assumptions: Dashboard may not provide adequate context or explanation of indicators

title: Potential non-compliance with health data regulations
description: Displaying inferred health conditions (eating-disorder, diabetes risk) may violate healthcare privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR health data provisions) if proper consent, data minimization, or security controls are not implemented.
assumptions: App may not have adequate legal basis for processing and displaying sensitive health inferences
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details

title: Unnecessary Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full health and location dataset is shared with external cloud provider, potentially exceeding data minimality requirements.
assumptions: Data sharing is necessary for analytics but may include more data than required.

title: Re-identification Risk from Health and Location Data
description: Sensitive health and location data may allow re-identification of individuals even if anonymized.
assumptions: Data may not be sufficiently anonymized before transfer.

title: Linkability of Health and Location Data
description: Data may be linked with other datasets at the cloud provider, increasing privacy risks.
assumptions: Cloud provider may combine data with other sources.

title: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Data at Cloud Provider
description: Cloud provider's security measures may be insufficient, leading to data breaches.
assumptions: Third-party security practices are not fully verified.
